response.sql: WITH state_totals AS (SELECT c.state_county_province AS st, COALESCE(SUM(ft.transaction_amount), 0) AS total FROM Financial_Transactions ft JOIN Invoices i ON i.invoice_number = ft.invoice_number JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.state_county_province), shares AS (SELECT st, total, total * 1.0 / SUM(total) OVER () AS share FROM state_totals), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS a FROM shares) SELECT SUM(s.total) AS combined_total, AVG(s.share) AS average_share, AVG(s.share - av.a) AS average_excess_over_average_share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share av WHERE s.share > av.a

assumptions.assumption: Customers with a NULL state_county_province form one group. An empty-string state would be a separate group, because I did not merge it with NULL.
A state whose transaction amounts are all NULL still counts as a state, with a total of 0. It is included in the average of shares.
The sum of all state totals is nonzero, so the shares are defined.
